site.title: ellipog
site.description: Manuals for the mods: how they work, how to configure them, and what the formats are.

/*sponsor: One affiliate arrangement, in the manifest because that is where the site's facts live — a link and a discount code written into a component would be a second place to keep in step. `code` is quoted verbatim on the page, and `url` carries the referral path.

sponsor.name: BisectHosting
sponsor./*badge: The small mark beside the host's name. `label` is what shows; `note` is the full phrase in the native tooltip, for a reader who wants to know what the mark means. The label is `Hosting partner`, and it was `Partner` alone until it was read beside the tagline it qualifies: `Minecraft server hosting` next to `PARTNER` says what the host does and that there is some arrangement, but not what the arrangement is about -- partner *of what*? `Hosting partner` carries both halves, so the chip states the relationship rather than leaving the tagline to imply it. Two alternatives were considered and dropped, and both are recorded here so they are not re-proposed: `Infrastructure` names a category this arrangement is not, and `Verified`/`Verified partner` claims a status the host does not confer -- BisectHosting's own material says `Partner Program` and `affiliate`, and never `verified`, so that word would be inventing a status, and a trust mark that overstates is worse than none. Change `label` to change the wording; nothing else needs touching.
sponsor./*logo: One mark, not two. It used to be a light and a dark SVG with CSS switching between them, but the glyph now takes its ink from `currentColor` and its knockouts from `var(--icon-ground)` -- so one file works on either ground and there is nothing left to switch. Generated by `bun run brand` from design/brand-source/, and committed like the mod icons. **This path is what `BrandMark` reads** -- it used to be written here and ignored, with the filename hardcoded in the component; with two marks in the band there would be two hardcoded names, so the manifest is the one place it is written now.
sponsor./*logoSize: The mark declares a viewBox of 243.7 by 81.21 and no width or height of its own, so these are the numbers the layout reserves before it is parsed. They match the viewBox ratio, which is why the width is 123 and not a round number -- and why BrandMark derives the width from them rather than the other way round. `logoHeight` is also the height it is drawn at, so the box is stated once and the component is not told it a second time.

/*support: The second cell in the band at the foot of every page: Ko-fi, where the mods' own running costs are tipped into. It is NOT a sponsorship and nothing about it is paid for -- so it carries no `rel="sponsored"`, no `Affiliate link` note, no badge, and its own landmark rather than the host's, because a region labelled `Sponsored` that also holds an unpaid tip jar is the misattribution the disclosure exists to prevent. `tagline` is what shows under the mark, and the handle beside it is derived from `url` rather than typed next to it, so the two cannot disagree. `logo`, `logoWidth` and `logoHeight` are the mark: the box it is drawn in, which `BrandMark` reads rather than being told, so `check.mjs` can hold the rendered box to these numbers. Deleting this object deletes the cell and the row falls back to one full-width cell.

support.name: Ko-fi
support./*logo: Generated by `bun run brand` from design/brand-source/kofi.svg -- Ko-fi's own wordmark, committed verbatim from their brand asset pack. Three quirks of that file are handled in the transform rather than by editing the source, and one of them is a dark-mode bug: its capsule and letterforms are the named colour `white`, which is this site's *ground*, so left named it renders as a white slab on a dark page while looking correct on a light one.
support./*logoSize: 124 by 34, and smaller than the host's 123 by 41 on purpose. The ratio is the file's (738 by 202, rounded to the pixel). The height is optical rather than arbitrary: the host's mark is a hexagon with a two-line wordmark inside it, so its ink fills about half its box, while Ko-fi's is one line of fat lettering that fills nearly all of it -- at the same 41px the tip jar out-weighed the cell it introduces. These two numbers are the box `BrandMark` draws and the ratio it derives the width from, so the size is one edit and the page cannot drift from it.

/*studio: Who engineers and maintains this site, and the one thing the colophon row at the foot of every page says. It is here rather than in the component for the same reason the sponsor is: the wording is a site fact, so changing it is one edit and the page cannot drift from it. `label` is quoted verbatim; `url` is the link AND the domain shown beside it, derived rather than typed twice, so the two cannot disagree.

author.bio: I build Minecraft mods. A couple are in development now; the rest are already out.

/*suite: ONLY MODS THAT EXIST. Every entry here is `status: "active"`, and `app/page.tsx` renders an entry only when it is -- so a mod is named on the site the day it is certain to ship and not before. A planned mod is not listed, not summarised, and not named anywhere in this repository: the idea is the thing being kept private, and a name plus a one-line summary is enough of it to be worth keeping. Those entries live in `design/planned/suite.json`, which is gitignored, and they move in here when the mod is certain. `check.mjs` asserts both halves of this -- that no entry is anything but active, and that the catalog says `planned` nowhere.

suite.name: Tenet
suite.summary: A visual questing engine that ships no questlines of its own. JSON files in, a pannable canvas out, and the server, not the client, decides what counts as done.

suite.name: Armature
suite.summary: A shared library mod. One loader seam, a strict JSON reader, and a client UI toolkit for layout, text, shapes, themes and widgets.

selected.name: Create Stellar
selected.summary: Create, with a progression line through it rather than an inventory of machines and no direction.

selected.name: Fairytale Origins
selected.summary: Eight storybook origins, each with a weakness that bites.
